title: Ask Claude to build a fun game from one prompt
summary: Simon Willison gave Claude's iPhone app one prompt for a tree game; he reports it worked 3 hours 7 minutes and returned a spot-the-difference game that is quite compelling.
agent_role: Claude designed and built the whole game from one prompt over a 3-hour-7-minute run; the human only wrote the prompt and published the result.
outcome: Author reports Claude returned a cosy spot-the-difference game with music, animation and achievements that is quite compelling to play.
what_they_did: Simon Willison used the regular Claude iPhone app, not the coding tool Claude Code, with Claude Opus 5.5 Max. He gave it one prompt: build a 3D web game called "Tree appreciator." It should show two computer-generated trees and be about appreciating their differences. He asked it to think hard about making it fun and beautiful, then published the result.
how_it_went: He reports Claude worked for 3 hours and 7 minutes. It returned a cosy spot-the-difference game with music, animation and achievements that he finds quite compelling to play.
worth_knowing: Willison says telling the model to "make sure it is fun" works uncomfortably well.
prompt: Build a three.js game called "[game name]" that shows [what the game displays] and whose core mechanic is [the idea, e.g. noticing differences between two generated objects]. Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful. Deliver it as a single HTML file I can open in a browser, and briefly explain the game rules and controls when you are done.

curation.rationale: A working, playable result with a shared transcript and a notable 3-hour autonomous run from a single prompt, but it is another agent-built game with little process detail.
